title: Chromebook will not turn on
steps: Connect the school-approved charger to the Chromebook and a permitted outlet.
Look for a charging light, if your model has one. Wait a few minutes.
Press the power button once. If there is still no sign of power, ask your teacher.
why: A drained battery may need time to charge. Never open the device or use a damaged charger.

title: Chromebook will not charge
steps: Check that the approved charger is firmly connected at both ends.
Look for visible damage without touching exposed wires. If the cable is damaged or hot, stop and tell your teacher.
Ask your teacher to test another approved charger if the battery icon still does not show charging.
why: Using the correct charger and intact cables matters.

title: Chromebook touchpad not working
steps: Make sure your fingers and touchpad are clean and dry.
Try sliding one finger across the touchpad and then tapping lightly.
If it still fails, ask your teacher before trying an approved external mouse.
why: Touchpads need clean, dry contact.

title: Right-click on a Chromebook
steps: Tap the touchpad with two fingers together.
Choose the menu item you need, or tap outside to close it.
why: A two-finger tap opens the context menu on most Chromebooks.

title: Take a Chromebook screenshot
steps: Press the Screenshot key if your keyboard has one, or Ctrl + Shift + Show windows.
Select the screenshot option (not video), then choose full screen or a selected area.
Take the capture and check the capture notification or Files > My files > Downloads. If your school chose a different location, ask your teacher.
why: The Show windows key typically looks like a rectangle with two lines beside it.

title: Chromebook screen too dark
steps: Press the brightness-up key on the top row a few times.
Check whether the device is awake by tapping a key. If the screen stays blank, ask your teacher.
why: Brightness is an everyday control, not an administrator setting.

title: Chromebook screen is sideways
steps: Stop and show your teacher the sideways display.
Ask them to restore the classroom's approved screen orientation.
why: Display settings can affect accessibility and classroom equipment; do not experiment with them.

title: Chromebook is frozen
steps: Wait a short time in case an app is still working.
Try switching to another open tab or window. Save work if the device responds.
If nothing responds, tell your teacher before restarting or forcing the device off.
why: A forced power-off can lose unsaved work.

title: Chromebook no sound
steps: Press volume-up once or twice. Keep the volume comfortable.
Check whether the video or tab has its own mute button.
If using an approved wired headset, check its plug. Ask your teacher if sound is still missing.
why: Device volume and app volume are separate.

title: Chromebook Wi-Fi problem
steps: Click the time area and look at the Wi-Fi icon without changing network settings.
Check whether the problem affects other approved class websites too.
Tell your teacher which approved network or website appears unavailable. Do not join another network without permission.
why: The teacher can distinguish a network outage from a device issue.

title: Find a Chromebook download
steps: Open the launcher and select Files.
Choose Downloads under My files. Look for the name or recent date.
Open the file only if it is one you recognize and are allowed to use.
why: Local Downloads and Google Drive are different locations.

title: Switch apps on Chromebook
steps: Press the Show windows key on the top row.
Click the window you want. You can also use Alt + Tab to switch between open windows.
why: Your work can be open behind another window.

title: Mouse not moving
steps: If wired, check that the mouse's USB plug is fully seated. If wireless, check its power switch and approved receiver.
Try moving the mouse on a plain, flat surface.
Ask your teacher to test an approved spare mouse. Do not unplug other students' devices.
why: The connection, surface or mouse power can prevent movement.

title: Switch mouse handedness
steps: With teacher permission, open Windows Settings and search for Mouse settings.
Find Primary mouse button and choose Left or Right as needed. If the option is blocked, ask your teacher.
Test a single click. Do not change other settings.
why: This is a specifically allowed example of a basic accessibility adjustment, subject to school rules.

title: Mouse scroll wheel not working
steps: Check whether you can scroll using the window's scrollbar.
Move the pointer over a scrollable part of the page and try the wheel again.
Ask your teacher to check the mouse if it fails in multiple apps.
why: Some panels capture scroll input differently.

title: Keyboard not responding
steps: Click inside a text field and try typing a harmless test word.
Check that your approved keyboard is connected securely.
Ask your teacher if the issue continues. Do not pull keys off or open the keyboard.
why: An inactive text field may make a working keyboard seem broken.

title: Number keypad not typing numbers
steps: Click in a text field and press Num Lock once.
Try typing a number on the keypad. If it does not work, ask your teacher.
why: Num Lock changes the keypad's usual behavior.

title: Letters are all capitalized
steps: Press Caps Lock once and test typing a letter.
Check that the Shift key is not being held down. Ask the teacher if a key is stuck.
why: Caps Lock and Shift affect letter capitalization.

title: Monitor is black
steps: Check the monitor's power light and press its power button if needed.
Look for loose visible cables without reaching behind heavy equipment. Ask the teacher to reconnect them.
Tell your teacher if the monitor shows No signal or remains black.
why: A monitor can be off even when the computer is running.

title: Headphones have no sound
steps: Check that your approved headset is plugged in fully or connected as your teacher showed you.
Check the headset's mute or volume control, then the app's volume.
Keep volume low while testing. Ask your teacher if sound is still missing.
why: Many headsets have their own controls.

title: Microphone does not work
steps: Check the headset or microphone's physical mute switch.
Check the mute button inside the approved app. Test only when your teacher permits recording.
If the app reports microphone access is blocked, ask your teacher instead of changing permissions.
why: Microphone access is controlled by the school and the app.

title: Webcam is not showing video
steps: Check for a physical camera cover and open it only with permission.
Check the camera button in the approved meeting or recording app.
If the app reports camera access is blocked, ask your teacher.
why: Camera privacy restrictions should not be bypassed.

title: USB device not recognized
steps: Use only a school-approved device. Check that its connector is securely seated and not damaged.
Open File Explorer if it is a storage device and look under This PC.
If it is still missing, ask your teacher. Never install drivers or format a drive.
why: A school policy or hardware issue may prevent USB devices from appearing.

title: Drawing tablet pen not working
steps: Check that the school tablet is connected and its pen is the correct one.
Open an approved drawing document and select a brush on an editable layer.
Ask the teacher if the pen still fails. Do not install tablet drivers.
why: A locked layer can look like a tablet problem.

title: Windows app is frozen
steps: Wait briefly while the app finishes processing.
If it responds, save your work immediately in the assigned location.
If it remains frozen, ask the teacher before closing or restarting it.
why: Closing an unresponsive program can lose work.

title: Take a Windows screenshot
steps: Press Windows + Shift + S.
Drag around the area you need, or choose the appropriate capture mode.
Open the capture notification if available, then save to your assigned folder or paste into the required document.
why: Capture only your own permitted work, not another student's information.

title: Find a minimized Windows app
steps: Look for the app's icon on the taskbar and click it.
Use Alt + Tab to cycle among open apps if necessary.
why: Minimizing does not close an app.

title: Printer did not print
steps: Confirm that your teacher has given permission to print.
Open print preview and check the assigned printer and page count.
If a job was already submitted, ask your teacher before sending it again.
why: Repeated printing wastes paper and can duplicate jobs.

title: Game controller not responding
steps: Check that the school-approved controller is connected as instructed.
Check whether the game has a controller option and that the intended game window is active.
Ask the teacher if there is still no response; do not install drivers or controller software.
why: Not every classroom game supports controllers.

title: Turn in an assignment
steps: Open the correct class and assignment in Google Classroom.
Check Your work and open the attachment to verify it is the correct completed file.
Select Turn in and confirm if prompted. If the assignment uses Mark as done, follow your teacher's directions.
why: Attaching a file is not always the same as submitting it.

title: Attach a file to an assignment
steps: Open the assignment and find Your work.
Choose Add or create, then choose Google Drive or File according to where your work is saved.
Select the correct file and verify it appears under Your work before turning in.
why: Use your own work and the file type requested by your teacher.

title: Turn in button shows an error
steps: Make sure you are in the correct class and assignment using your school account.
Check whether all required attachments finished loading. Do not repeatedly click Turn in.
Tell your teacher the exact error message without sharing passwords or personal details.
why: Some submission errors need teacher action.

title: Find teacher feedback
steps: Open your class and the relevant assignment.
Look for the returned grade, rubric, or private comments if available.
Read the teacher's instructions before changing or resubmitting work.
why: Returned work may include specific correction instructions.

title: Resubmit corrected work
steps: Check that your teacher allows corrections and resubmission.
Open the original assignment and follow your teacher's directions for updating the existing file or attachment.
If available and permitted, submit the corrected work again and confirm the status.
why: Resubmission can affect the recorded submission time.

title: Find a missing assignment
steps: Open the correct class and select Classwork.
Look under the topic or date your teacher named. Check your assignment list if available.
If it is missing, tell your teacher which assignment you are looking for.
why: Classwork is often organized by topic rather than date.

title: Find a Google Drive file
steps: Open Google Drive using your school account.
Search for part of the filename, or look in Recent or Shared with me if appropriate.
Open the matching file and verify the title and owner before editing.
why: A shared file may not appear in My Drive.

title: File says access denied
steps: Check whether you are using the school account that was assigned the file.
Return to the original classroom link and try opening it once more.
Tell your teacher if access is still blocked. Do not try another student's account or change sharing permissions.
why: The file owner or school controls access.

title: Rename a file
steps: Open your own file or select it in the file browser.
Use the title field or Rename command and enter the filename your teacher requested.
Keep the original file extension when using a file browser.
why: Clear filenames make your work easier to find.

title: Make a copy of a Google file
steps: Check your teacher's instructions and make sure copying is allowed.
In a Google document, use File > Make a copy if available.
Name the copy and save it in the assigned location.
why: A copy is separate from the original and may not be automatically attached in Classroom.

title: Find a Windows download
steps: Open File Explorer using its folder icon or Windows + E.
Select Downloads and look for the file by name or date.
If it is not there, check the browser's download list with Ctrl + J.
why: The browser and the file browser can help locate downloads.

title: Understand file types
aliases: png jpg psd ai pdf zip
steps: Look at the end of the filename or its displayed type.
PNG and JPG are images; PSD and AI are editable Adobe project formats; PDF is a document; ZIP is an archive.
Use the exact format requested by your teacher. Renaming an extension does not convert a file.
why: Exporting actually converts a file to a different format.

title: Open a ZIP file
steps: Use only a trusted ZIP supplied by your teacher.
On Windows, right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All. On Chromebook, open it in Files and copy the required contents into an assigned folder.
Open the extracted files rather than trying to edit them inside the archive.
why: A ZIP is a container; files often need to be extracted first.

title: Save work in the correct folder
steps: In your app, choose Save or Save As as appropriate.
Select the teacher-approved folder and use the requested filename.
Check the location in File Explorer or Files after saving.
why: A successful save is not the same as a Classroom submission.

title: Google Docs text formatting
steps: Select the text you want to format, or place the cursor before typing.
Use the toolbar to choose the required font, size or style.
Check that the result is readable and follows your assignment directions.
why: Formatting changes appearance, not the content of your work.

title: Google Docs page break
steps: Place the cursor where a new page should begin.
Use Insert > Break > Page break if the document is in Pages mode.
If the option is missing, ask your teacher whether the document uses pageless mode.
why: A page break is more reliable than many empty lines.

title: Insert image in Google Docs
steps: Place the cursor where the approved image belongs.
Choose Insert > Image and select the permitted source.
Select the file and resize using a corner handle as needed.
why: Choose an image you have permission to use.

title: Google Slides presentation mode
steps: Open the correct presentation.
Choose Slideshow near the top of the editor.
Use arrow keys to move between slides and Escape to leave presentation mode.
why: Presenting is different from editing the slides.

title: Google Slides crop a picture
steps: Select the image on your slide.
Click the crop tool and drag the crop handles to hide unwanted edges.
Press Enter or click outside to finish.
why: Cropping changes the visible area rather than merely stretching the picture.

title: Add a Google Slides text box
steps: Choose Insert > Text box or the text box tool.
Click or drag on the slide to place a text box.
Type your own text and adjust size or alignment using the toolbar.
why: TechGuide can explain the tool but cannot write your text.

title: Google Sheets formula not working
steps: Select the cell and look at the formula bar.
Check that formulas begin with an equals sign and that any cell references and parentheses are correct.
Compare the syntax with the example supplied by your teacher. Ask for help if the error continues.
why: The syntax matters; TechGuide will not solve assignment calculations.

title: Google Sheets cell text is cut off
steps: Select the affected cell or cells.
Use the text wrapping control in the toolbar and choose Wrap if appropriate.
If needed, resize the column by dragging its header boundary.
why: Wrapping can make long text visible without changing the text itself.

title: Google Forms cannot submit
steps: Look for required questions marked with an asterisk or an error message.
Complete your own required responses and check any formatting instructions.
If the form is closed or access is denied, ask the teacher.
why: Required fields must be complete before the form accepts a response.

title: Google Meet audio or camera
steps: Check the microphone and camera buttons in the meeting controls.
Check your approved headset and any physical camera cover.
Ask your teacher if access is blocked; do not change browser permissions.
why: School-managed permissions must be respected.

title: Website will not load
steps: Check the address or open the link your teacher provided.
Reload once if you have no unsaved form responses. Try another approved class site to see whether the issue is widespread.
If a page is blocked or still unavailable, ask your teacher.
why: A loading error may be a website, connection or school policy issue.

title: Browser page looks too big or small
steps: With the browser active, use Ctrl + 0 to return the page to its normal zoom if you do not need a particular accessibility zoom.
Use Ctrl + plus or Ctrl + minus only for a comfortable reading size.
If the whole device display is affected, ask your teacher rather than changing system settings.
why: Browser zoom is separate from system display scaling.

title: Reopen an accidentally closed tab
steps: Press Ctrl + Shift + T in Chrome.
Check that the reopened page is the one you need. Unsaved form content may not return.
why: The browser may remember recently closed tabs.

title: Browser full screen stuck
steps: On Windows, try F11 once. On a Chromebook, use the top-row full-screen key.
If a video is full-screen instead, try Escape.
why: Browser full-screen and video full-screen are different modes.

title: Website is blocked by school
steps: Stop at the block page.
Tell your teacher the approved educational site you were trying to use.
Wait for staff to review access. Do not attempt another address, proxy or method to evade the restriction.
why: Only authorized staff can review school access restrictions.

title: Suspicious pop-up or message
steps: Do not click the alert, call a number, download anything or enter information.
If safe to do so, close the ordinary browser tab without interacting with the alert.
Tell your teacher immediately, especially if you clicked or entered any information.
why: Fake alerts often try to pressure people into unsafe actions.

title: Forgot school password
steps: Check that you are using the correct school sign-in page and that Caps Lock is not on.
If you still cannot sign in, ask your teacher or school-approved support staff.
Never type your password into TechGuide or share it with another student.
why: Account recovery is handled through the school's approved process.

title: Photoshop Layers panel is missing
steps: In Photoshop, open the Window menu.
Choose Layers to show the Layers panel.
Select the layer you intend to work on and check whether it is visible.
why: Panels can be closed without deleting the document's layers.

title: Photoshop brush will not paint
steps: Select the Brush tool and an editable layer in the Layers panel. Check whether the layer is visible and locked.
Check brush size, foreground color and opacity in the options bar. If a mask is selected, check whether you meant to select its image thumbnail instead.
If a selection is active, painting may be limited to that area. Deselect with Ctrl + D only if you no longer need the selection.
why: Layer state, selections and brush options all affect painting.

title: Remove moving dotted selection lines
steps: Save your work if needed.
If you are finished with the current selection, choose Select > Deselect or press Ctrl + D.
Check that the moving outline is gone before working on a different area.
why: The dotted boundary marks the selected area; deselecting does not delete the pixels.

title: Photoshop image will not move
steps: Select the Move tool and the intended layer in the Layers panel.
Check for a lock icon and make sure you selected the correct object.
If the layer is locked intentionally or is a special background layer, ask the teacher before changing it.
why: The Move tool moves the selected layer or object.

title: Photoshop picture disappeared
steps: Check the eye icon beside the intended layer in the Layers panel.
Check whether another opaque layer is above it or the layer opacity is zero.
Use undo only if you just made an unintended change. Do not delete layers to find the image.
why: Hidden or covered layers may still exist.

title: Photoshop text is hard to see
steps: Select the text layer and make sure its visibility is on.
Use the Type tool to check text size and color against the background.
Check that the text layer is above the intended background layer.
why: Text needs contrast and the correct layer order.

title: Add a stroke to Photoshop text
aliases: how to put an outline on text
steps: Select the text layer in the Layers panel.
Open the Layer Style menu using the fx button and choose Stroke.
Choose a readable color and size, preview it, then confirm.
why: A stroke outlines the text while keeping the text layer editable.

title: Export a Photoshop PNG or JPG
steps: Save the editable PSD project first.
Choose File > Export > Export As and choose PNG or JPG as required.
Check the preview, export to the assigned folder and verify the exported file opens.
why: PNG can preserve transparency; JPG does not. Keep the editable PSD separately.

title: Save a Photoshop PSD
steps: Choose File > Save As when creating the named project file.
Choose Photoshop (PSD) if available and select your assigned folder.
Save and verify the filename. Keep your layers intact.
why: A PSD preserves editable Photoshop features better than an exported JPG.

title: Photoshop eraser not working
steps: Check that the intended layer is selected, visible and editable.
Check whether you selected the image thumbnail rather than a layer mask. Check eraser size and opacity.
If the layer is a Smart Object or locked, ask your teacher before converting it. Use a mask if that is the assigned technique.
why: Erasing pixels can be destructive; a mask may be safer.

title: Photoshop image looks pixelated
steps: Check the document zoom; view it at 100% to judge actual pixels.
Check whether the source image was small or enlarged a lot.
Ask your teacher for an approved higher-resolution source if needed.
why: Zoom and source resolution are different; enlarging does not restore lost detail.

title: Photoshop layer mask basics
steps: Select the layer and its mask thumbnail, if the layer already has a mask.
Paint black on the mask to hide and white to reveal; use a small test area first.
Select the image thumbnail again when you want to edit the image rather than the mask.
why: Masks hide pixels without permanently erasing them.

title: Change part of a photo's color
steps: Select only the intended area using an appropriate selection tool.
Add a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer using the Adjustments panel or Layer menu.
Adjust hue and saturation, then refine the mask if the color affects unwanted areas.
why: An adjustment layer allows you to revise the color without permanently changing the original.

title: Illustrator tools or panels missing
steps: Open the Window menu and look for the named panel, such as Layers or Properties.
Choose the panel to show it. If the toolbar is missing, look under Window > Toolbars for the appropriate toolbar.
Ask the teacher if your classroom workspace is different.
why: Panels and toolbars can be hidden without removing your artwork.

title: Fill and stroke are mixed up
steps: Select your intended object with the Selection tool.
In the toolbar or Properties panel, select Fill for the interior color or Stroke for the outline.
Choose the color and adjust stroke weight if needed.
why: Fill and stroke are independent object attributes.

title: Illustrator object will not move
steps: Choose the black-arrow Selection tool and click the intended object.
Check the Layers panel for a lock or hidden object. Do not unlock items the teacher intentionally locked.
If a different object is selected, click away and select the correct one.
why: The white-arrow Direct Selection tool edits individual points instead of the whole object.

title: Make a shape in Illustrator
steps: Choose Rectangle, Ellipse or another approved shape tool from the toolbar.
Click and drag on the artboard. Hold Shift for a square or circle when appropriate.
Adjust fill and stroke in the Properties panel.
why: Vector shapes can be resized without the same pixelation as a raster photo.

title: Illustrator text tool
steps: Choose the Type tool and click on the artboard.
Type your own words and select the text to adjust its font, size and color.
Switch to the Selection tool to move the text object.
why: TechGuide explains the tool, not what to write.

title: Align objects in Illustrator
steps: Select the objects you want to align.
Open Window > Align if the Align controls are not visible.
Check the Align To option, then choose the alignment or distribution needed.
why: Aligning to the artboard is different from aligning to other selected objects.

title: Illustrator Shape Builder basics
steps: Select the overlapping editable shapes you want to work with.
Choose the Shape Builder tool and drag across regions you want to combine.
Review the result and use undo if you joined the wrong regions.
why: Shape Builder works with selected shapes and their overlapping regions.

title: Illustrator artboard is too small
steps: Check the dimensions required by the assignment.
Choose the Artboard tool and select the correct artboard.
Adjust width and height using available artboard controls, then return to the Selection tool.
why: Resizing an artboard is not the same as resizing the artwork.

title: Illustrator export PNG or JPG
steps: Save your editable AI document first.
Use File > Export > Export As, choose PNG or JPG and select Use Artboards if needed for the assigned crop.
Choose the requested options, export to your assigned folder and verify the file.
why: An exported image does not replace your editable AI project.

title: Illustrator save editable AI file
steps: Choose File > Save As when naming the project.
Select Adobe Illustrator (AI) as the format and choose your assigned folder.
Save and verify the filename before exporting other formats.
why: The AI file keeps your editable objects.

title: Illustrator artwork appears as outlines
steps: Look at the View menu to see whether Preview is available.
Choose Preview if you accidentally switched to Outline mode, or use Ctrl + Y to toggle when appropriate.
Check that your colors return. Ask your teacher if they do not.
why: Outline mode shows paths rather than the filled appearance of artwork.

title: Illustrator object behind another object
steps: Select the intended object using the Selection tool or Layers panel.
Use Object > Arrange and choose the needed stacking change, such as Bring to Front.
Check the result without deleting the other artwork.
why: Objects higher in the stacking order may cover objects below them.

title: PlayForge game will not load
steps: Check that the teacher has allowed the game or tool at this time.
Return to the PlayForge page and try opening the approved app once more. Avoid reloading if you have unsaved work.
Tell your teacher which game and what appears on screen.
why: Some apps require a first online load and school policy may restrict access.

title: PlayForge saved progress is missing
steps: Check whether you are using the same browser profile and device as before.
If the app supports import, ask your teacher about restoring your own exported backup.
Do not clear browser data or change account settings to recover progress.
why: Many PlayForge apps save locally and do not automatically sync across devices.

title: Chromebook battery drains quickly
aliases: chromebook battery low all the time
steps: Save your current work and check the battery icon by the clock.
Close tabs you no longer need and lower brightness to a comfortable level.
If the battery still drains unusually fast, tell your teacher.
why: Open pages and bright screens consume energy; persistent rapid drain may need service.

title: Chromebook charger only works at an angle
steps: Stop moving the plug around and set the device on a flat surface.
Tell your teacher the charging connection is intermittent; do not force the plug.
why: A loose port or lead can be damaged further by movement.

title: Chromebook feels unusually hot
steps: Stop using it and tell your teacher, especially if it is too hot to touch.
Keep it away from paper, fabric and other flammable materials without handling a dangerously hot device.
why: Heat can indicate blocked airflow or a hardware problem.

title: Liquid spilled on Chromebook
steps: Stop using the Chromebook and alert an adult immediately.
Do not charge it, turn it on again, shake it or try to dry it with heat.
why: Liquid can damage electrical components even when the outside appears dry.

title: Chromebook dropped or cracked
steps: Stop using the device if the case, glass or hinges are damaged.
Report what happened to your teacher; do not press on broken glass or attempt repairs.
why: Physical damage can create a safety hazard.

title: Chromebook lid or hinge is stuck
steps: Set the Chromebook on a level surface.
Do not pull harder or force the lid; ask your teacher to inspect it.
why: Forcing a hinge can break the display cable or case.

title: Chromebook wakes to sign-in screen
steps: Use your own school account on the sign-in screen.
If you cannot sign in, ask your teacher; do not use somebody else's account.
why: Closing the lid or inactivity can lock a managed device.

title: Chromebook going to sleep during work
steps: Tap a key or the touchpad to wake the screen.
Save or submit your work regularly; tell the teacher if sleep interrupts a required activity.
why: School-managed sleep rules are not a student setting to change.

title: Safely shut down a Chromebook
steps: Save open work and check that uploads are finished.
With teacher permission, select the clock and the power icon to shut down.
If the device is unresponsive, ask the teacher instead of forcing a shutdown.
why: A normal shutdown lets apps finish their work.

title: Safely restart a Chromebook
steps: Save open work and tell your teacher why a restart is needed.
With permission, use the clock's power menu to shut down normally, then turn it back on.
Reopen only the needed apps and check whether the issue is gone.
why: A restart can clear temporary problems but unsaved work may be lost.

title: Chromebook screen too bright
steps: Use the brightness-down key on the top row until the display is comfortable.
If visibility still causes problems, ask your teacher about approved accommodations.
why: Brightness is an ordinary display control.

title: Chromebook screen flickers
steps: Stop looking at the display if flashing causes discomfort.
Save work if safe and tell your teacher; do not change display drivers or settings.
why: Flicker can be a display or software fault.

title: Only one app is blank
steps: Check whether another open app is visible.
Save work if available and reopen only the affected app with permission.
If several apps are blank, tell your teacher.
why: This helps separate an app error from a screen problem.

title: Chromebook browser text too large
steps: With Chrome active, press Ctrl + 0 to restore the page's usual zoom if no accommodation requires a different level.
Use Ctrl + minus to reduce page zoom only as needed.
If the entire desktop is enlarged, ask your teacher.
why: Page zoom affects the webpage rather than other apps.

title: Chromebook browser text too small
steps: In Chrome, press Ctrl + plus to enlarge the page.
Use Ctrl + 0 to return to normal when appropriate.
Ask for help if you need an ongoing accessibility adjustment.
why: Page zoom is a reversible reading control.

title: Chromebook entire desktop is enlarged
steps: Check whether the shelf and clock are also enlarged, not just a website.
If they are, ask your teacher to check magnification or approved accessibility controls; do not turn them off yourself.
why: System magnification is different from webpage zoom and may be an accommodation.

title: Chromebook window is full screen
steps: Try the full-screen key on the top row in the active app.
If a video is full screen, try Esc.
If the app is intentionally locked for testing, ask your teacher rather than trying to exit.
why: Full-screen view hides some controls.

title: Chromebook maximize a window
steps: Click the square button near the upper-right corner of the window.
Click the same control again when you need the previous size.
why: Maximizing uses the available display area.

title: Chromebook minimize a window
steps: Click the dash near the upper-right corner of the window.
Select the app's icon on the shelf to bring it back.
why: Minimize hides the window without closing it.

title: Chromebook close an app safely
steps: Save your changes first.
Click the X in the upper-right corner of the intended window; check that it is not a different app.
why: Closing a window may close unsaved work.

title: Chromebook view all open windows
steps: Press the Show windows key (rectangle with lines) on the top row.
Select the window you want to return to.
why: Overview helps locate open work without closing anything.

title: Chromebook split screen two apps
steps: Open the two apps you need and make sure both allow resizing.
Drag the first window by its title bar to a screen edge until a preview appears, then release.
Select or drag the second window to the other side.
why: Side-by-side windows make it easier to follow directions while working.

title: Chromebook missing shelf
steps: Move the pointer to the bottom edge of the display and see whether the shelf appears.
If a video or ordinary app is full screen, exit its full-screen view.
If it remains hidden, ask your teacher rather than altering shelf settings.
why: The shelf can be hidden by full-screen apps or managed preferences.

title: Chromebook open an app from Launcher
steps: Press the Launcher or Search key, usually where Caps Lock is on other keyboards.
Type the name of an approved app and select its result.
If the app is unavailable, ask your teacher; do not install it yourself.
why: The Launcher searches available apps.

title: Chromebook move a window
steps: Restore the window from maximized view if needed.
Drag an empty part of its title bar to the desired place.
why: Moving a window does not alter its contents.

title: Chromebook resize a window
steps: Move the pointer to a window edge or corner until it changes shape.
Drag gently to the needed size; if the app does not resize, use its maximize control.
why: Some apps impose minimum window sizes.

title: Chromebook Caps Lock is on
steps: Look for an uppercase typing indicator.
On many Chromebooks, Alt + Launcher toggles Caps Lock; if your keyboard has a dedicated Caps Lock key, use it instead.
Type a test letter in your own document.
why: Caps Lock affects letters until it is turned off.

title: Chromebook letters typed are wrong
steps: Try a few letters in your own document without holding Shift or other keys.
Look for a language or keyboard indicator near the clock if present.
Ask your teacher to restore the approved keyboard layout if needed.
why: A different layout or held modifier can change the characters typed.

title: Chromebook key is physically stuck
steps: Stop pressing the affected key and check for visible debris without using tools.
Tell the teacher; do not pull off keycaps or pour cleaner on the keyboard.
why: Forcing a key can damage the keyboard.

title: Chromebook keyboard completely unresponsive
steps: Check whether the pointer still works and whether a different approved app accepts typing.
If only one app fails, save and reopen it if possible.
If all apps fail, ask your teacher.
why: Testing another app helps identify whether this is a keyboard fault.

title: Chromebook Backspace and Delete
steps: Use Backspace to remove the character before the cursor.
In an editable text field, Alt + Backspace usually deletes the character after the cursor.
Use these only on your own text, not on unfamiliar files.
why: The two actions delete in opposite directions.

title: Chromebook type a capital letter
steps: Hold Shift while pressing the letter you want to capitalize.
Release Shift to continue typing normally.
why: Shift changes a single keystroke without keeping Caps Lock on.

title: Chromebook copy text
aliases: how do i copy and paste
steps: Select your own text or a teacher-approved item.
Press Ctrl + C to copy it.
To paste the copied text, click inside an approved destination and press Ctrl + V.
why: Copying leaves the original in place.

title: Chromebook paste text
steps: Click where the copied content belongs.
Press Ctrl + V; check that the result is what you intended.
why: The clipboard holds the most recent copied item.

title: Chromebook paste without formatting
steps: In a supported browser text editor, click the destination.
Press Ctrl + Shift + V where supported and verify the pasted content.
If unsupported, use the editor's paste-without-formatting option if provided.
why: This avoids importing unwanted source formatting.

title: Chromebook cut and move text
steps: Select text you own and press Ctrl + X.
Click the new location and press Ctrl + V; undo if you moved the wrong content.
why: Cut removes the selection from its old location.

title: Chromebook undo a mistake
steps: Keep the affected document active.
Press Ctrl + Z once and inspect the result before repeating.
why: Undo reverses recent edits in many apps.

title: Chromebook redo an edit
steps: Use the current app's Edit menu and look for Redo.
In many editors Ctrl + Shift + Z also works; verify the result.
why: Redo restores an action you recently undid.

title: Chromebook select all text
steps: Click inside the text area you want to work with.
Press Ctrl + A and inspect what is selected before doing anything else.
why: Selection depends on which app or field has focus.

title: Chromebook find a word
steps: Open the page or document you want to search.
Press Ctrl + F, enter the word and use the arrows to move between matches.
Press Esc when finished.
why: Find locates existing text without changing it.

title: Chromebook move through form fields
steps: Press Tab to move to the next available control.
Press Shift + Tab to move backward; check the highlighted control before typing.
why: Keyboard navigation can help when a mouse is inconvenient.

title: Chromebook open keyboard shortcut help
steps: Press Ctrl + Launcher + S if supported to open the keyboard shortcut viewer.
Search for the action you need, without editing shortcut assignments.
If the shortcut viewer is unavailable, ask your teacher.
why: The viewer shows shortcuts supported by the device.

title: Chromebook touchpad scroll
steps: Rest two fingers on the touchpad and move them together up or down.
If the page does not scroll, point into the scrollable part of the page and try again.
why: Scrolling works only where content extends beyond the visible area.

title: Chromebook touchpad click and drag
steps: Point at the item and hold the touchpad click with one finger.
Move another finger to drag the item, then release at the destination.
If this is a file, check the destination before dropping it.
why: Dragging moves or repositions selected items.

title: Chromebook touchpad pointer jumps
steps: Use one finger and keep your palm away from the touchpad.
Check that your hands and the surface are dry; if the problem continues, tell your teacher.
why: Extra contact can cause unexpected pointer movement.

title: Chromebook touchscreen not responding
steps: Confirm that the model actually has a touchscreen.
Try the touchpad and check whether the app is still responding.
Ask your teacher if the screen should accept touch but does not.
why: Not all Chromebook displays are touch-enabled.

title: Chromebook touchscreen zoom
steps: In an ordinary supported page, place two fingers on the touchscreen and move them apart or together.
If this does not work, use the app's zoom controls rather than changing system settings.
why: Touch gestures vary by app and model.

title: Chromebook open a new browser tab
steps: With Chrome active, press Ctrl + T or click the plus next to the tabs.
Enter a teacher-approved address or open a class resource.
why: A tab opens another page in the same window.

title: Chromebook close one browser tab
steps: Check that the tab has no unsaved form or assignment changes.
Click its X or press Ctrl + W while that tab is active.
Other tabs should remain open unless this was the last tab.
why: Closing a tab is not the same as closing all Chrome windows.

title: Chromebook move between browser tabs
steps: Click the tab you need or press Ctrl + Tab to move forward.
Use Ctrl + Shift + Tab to move backward.
why: Tabs allow you to switch pages without reopening them.

title: Chromebook reopen last closed tab
steps: With Chrome open, press Ctrl + Shift + T.
Check that the restored page is the one you need; unsaved form contents might not return.
why: Chrome may restore the page but not every unsaved edit.

title: Chromebook refresh a webpage
steps: Save anything you have typed if possible.
Click Chrome's reload arrow or press Ctrl + R once.
If the page still fails, note the error and ask your teacher.
why: Reloading requests a fresh copy of the page and can lose unsaved form input.

title: Chromebook go back to previous webpage
steps: Click the browser Back arrow near the address bar.
If the page warns about unsaved changes, cancel and save your work first.
why: Back returns to a prior page in the current tab.

title: Chromebook go forward to webpage
steps: After using Back, look for the Forward arrow near the address bar.
Click it if available; save any unsaved input before navigating.
why: Forward revisits a page you moved back from.

title: Chromebook address bar search
steps: Click in the bar at the top of Chrome or press Ctrl + L.
Enter the exact school-approved web address or search phrase and press Enter.
why: The address bar supports both web addresses and searches.

title: Chromebook save a class bookmark
steps: Open the class webpage and click the star in the address bar if available.
Keep a clear name and choose an approved bookmark folder, then confirm.
why: Bookmarks make it easier to return to a page later.

title: Chromebook find existing bookmarks
steps: Open Chrome's three-dot menu and look for Bookmarks and lists or Bookmarks.
Choose your saved class link, without editing managed bookmarks.
why: Bookmarks store links rather than copies of pages.

title: Chromebook browser shows download list
steps: Open Chrome and press Ctrl + J.
Locate the expected file and use Show in folder if available.
Do not open unknown downloads.
why: The downloads list can identify where a file was saved.

title: Chromebook link opens wrong tab
steps: Look along the top of Chrome for a new tab, including narrow tabs.
Select the tab with the matching page title.
If it opened a new window, use the Show windows key.
why: Links may open outside the current tab.

title: Chromebook too many tabs slow browser
steps: Save work on any tabs you are not using.
Close unnecessary tabs one at a time, keeping the class assignment open.
If the browser is still slow, ask your teacher before restarting.
why: Each tab can consume memory and processing time.

title: Chromebook text cursor not in typing box
steps: Click directly inside the teacher-assigned text field.
Look for a blinking cursor and try a short test in your own work.
If the field is disabled or read-only, ask the teacher.
why: The page must focus an editable field to receive typing.

title: Chromebook page asks to enable pop-ups
steps: Check whether the message comes from an expected class site.
Ask your teacher to verify whether the pop-up is needed; do not change browser permissions.
why: A blocked pop-up may be a protection or school policy.

title: Chromebook website certificate warning
steps: Stop before entering any login information.
Show the warning and website address to your teacher; do not click through the warning.
why: Certificate warnings can indicate an unsafe or misconfigured connection.

title: Chromebook open Files app
steps: Press Launcher and search for Files.
Open the Files app and select My files or Google Drive as appropriate.
why: Files shows device storage and available connected school storage.

title: Chromebook create a folder
steps: Open Files and navigate to a folder where you are allowed to create files.
Right-click an empty area, choose New folder and give it a clear class-related name.
why: Folders organize files without changing their contents.

title: Chromebook rename own file
steps: In Files, locate the file you created.
Open its context menu, choose Rename and type a clear name; keep the original file extension if shown.
why: Changing a file extension does not convert its format.

title: Chromebook copy a file
steps: Select the file you own in Files and press Ctrl + C.
Open the approved destination and press Ctrl + V; confirm both copies exist.
why: Copying preserves the original file.

title: Chromebook move a file to folder
steps: Locate your own file in Files and press Ctrl + X.
Open the intended folder and press Ctrl + V; check that it is in the new location.
If moving to Drive, wait for the upload or sync to finish.
why: Moving changes the location of a file.

title: Chromebook preview a file
steps: Select a known file in the Files app.
Press Space to preview it if supported, then Esc to dismiss the preview.
why: A preview is useful for identifying a file before using it.

title: Chromebook search for a local file
steps: Open Files and choose the location where you last saved the work.
Use its search control to enter part of the filename and inspect matching files.
Check the filename and location before submitting anything.
why: Searching within the likely location narrows results.

title: Chromebook sort downloaded files
steps: Open Files and select Downloads under My files.
In list view, click the date or name column if present; otherwise use the sort control.
Look for the expected file rather than opening unknown ones.
why: Sorting by date helps locate recently saved work.

title: Chromebook select several files
steps: Open Files and select the first file.
Hold Ctrl while clicking additional files you own; verify all selected items are intended.
why: Selecting several files makes it easier to upload or organize them together.

title: Chromebook extract a ZIP archive
steps: Only use an archive from an approved class source.
Open the ZIP in Files, select the required files, and copy them to an approved folder; an Extract all option may also be available.
Open the copied folder to verify the usable files are there.
why: A ZIP is a container; some apps need extracted files.

title: Chromebook make a ZIP of class work
steps: In Files, select only the files or folder your teacher requested.
Open the context menu and select Zip selection if available.
Confirm the archive name and contents before submitting.
why: A ZIP bundles multiple files together.

title: Chromebook local file versus Google Drive
steps: Open Files and identify whether the file is under My files or Google Drive.
If the teacher wants a cloud copy, copy your file into the correct school Drive folder and wait for sync.
why: Local files may not appear on a different Chromebook.

title: Chromebook Drive file is offline
steps: Check whether the Chromebook has the approved network connection.
If a file was already made available offline, try opening it from the permitted Drive location.
If not available, tell your teacher and wait for connectivity; do not change sync settings.
why: Offline access is not available for every cloud file.

title: Chromebook file will not open
steps: Check the filename extension, such as PDF, PNG or ZIP.
If it is an approved file, try the provided viewer or ask your teacher which program is intended.
Do not install an app or change the extension to force it open.
why: Different file types need compatible apps.

title: Chromebook storage is full
steps: Save important work to its approved location if possible.
Tell your teacher the storage warning; do not delete unfamiliar files, apps or browser data.
why: Low local space can prevent saving and downloading.

title: Chromebook file has duplicate name
steps: Check the full filename and modified date of the copies.
Preview the known files to identify the correct version and rename your own file clearly if necessary.
why: Repeated downloads can create numbered copies.

title: Chromebook upload a local file
steps: Open the teacher-assigned upload page and select its file picker.
Navigate to My files > Downloads or the correct Drive folder, select the intended file and confirm.
Wait for the upload to finish before closing the tab.
why: Selecting a file is not the same as finishing its upload.

title: Chromebook download has not finished
steps: Check Chrome's downloads list for progress or an error.
Keep the tab open if the website requires it and wait briefly on the approved network.
If it fails, report the error rather than clicking repeated download buttons.
why: Large files can take time or require a stable connection.

title: Chromebook screenshot only part of screen
steps: Open Screen capture with the Screenshot key or Ctrl + Shift + Show windows.
Select screenshot and partial-screen mode, then drag around only the needed area.
Capture and locate it in Files or the capture notification; avoid private information.
why: A partial capture excludes unrelated information.

title: Chromebook screenshot only one window
steps: Open Screen capture with the Screenshot key or Ctrl + Shift + Show windows.
Choose screenshot and window mode, then select the approved window.
Check the resulting image before sharing.
why: Window capture helps keep other apps out of the image.

title: Chromebook screenshot not found
steps: Check the capture notification if it is still visible.
Open Files > My files > Downloads and look for the recent image; ask your teacher if a different location was configured.
why: Captures normally save to a local folder and can also appear in a notification.

title: Chromebook screenshot saved as video
steps: Open Screen capture and check whether video recording was selected instead of screenshot.
If a recording is running, stop it with the recording control on the shelf.
Choose screenshot mode and capture only teacher-approved content.
why: Screenshots are still images; recordings are video files.

title: Chromebook screen recording for class
steps: Get teacher permission and close any private content, messages or other students' work.
Open Screen capture and choose video with the approved capture area; do not record others without permission.
Stop using the shelf recording control when done and inspect the file before submitting.
why: Screen recordings can expose personal information and should be intentional.

title: Chromebook volume too quiet
steps: Use the volume-up key to raise sound gradually to a comfortable level.
Check the volume in the class video or app itself.
If it is still quiet, ask your teacher to test approved headphones.
why: Device and app volume are separate controls.

title: Chromebook volume muted
steps: Check whether the speaker icon shows mute and use the volume key to restore a low comfortable level.
Check whether the class video is separately muted.
Only unmute when sound is permitted in class.
why: Muted audio may be controlled by the device or the app.

title: Chromebook sound comes from speakers instead of headphones
steps: Reduce volume first and check that the approved headphone plug is fully seated.
If required, show the audio output choices in the clock panel to your teacher; let them choose the approved output.
why: Audio can be routed to a connected device or the built-in speakers.

title: Chromebook headphones sound only on one side
steps: Check the headphone connection and adjust the headset comfortably.
Try an approved spare headset with permission; do not change accessibility audio balance.
If the problem follows the device, report it to your teacher.
why: A cable or headset fault can affect one channel.

title: Chromebook headphone plug will not fit
steps: Check whether the approved headphones use a compatible audio or USB connection.
Never force a connector; ask the teacher for an approved headset or adapter.
why: Ports have different shapes and purposes.

title: Chromebook Bluetooth headset not connecting
steps: Check whether the school permits this headset and whether it is charged.
Ask your teacher to check pairing; do not connect unknown devices or change Bluetooth settings.
why: Wireless accessories may need approved pairing and school policies may restrict it.

title: Chromebook microphone muted in class app
steps: In the assigned call or recording app, look for its microphone icon.
Unmute only when the teacher requests speaking or recording, and test briefly.
If the control is unavailable, tell your teacher.
why: App mute prevents audio capture without changing system settings.

title: Chromebook microphone not detecting voice
steps: Check that the approved headset microphone is connected and any physical mute switch is off.
In the assigned app, check whether its microphone is muted.
If permission or input choice is needed, ask your teacher.
why: A physical mute switch and app mute can both block sound.

title: Chromebook microphone permission denied
steps: Confirm the website is the teacher-assigned resource.
Show the permission warning to your teacher; do not grant or change browser permissions yourself.
why: Microphone access may be intentionally restricted.

title: Chromebook camera black image
steps: Check for an ordinary physical privacy shutter and open it only when your teacher requires camera use.
Look for the app's camera-off icon and enable video only for the assigned task.
If the screen stays black, tell your teacher.
why: A closed shutter or app camera control can hide video.

title: Chromebook camera permission denied
steps: Verify that the app is an approved class resource.
Show the permission message to your teacher and do not change browser permissions.
why: Camera access is sensitive and may be managed by school IT.

title: Chromebook video plays but stutters
steps: Pause briefly to let the class video load if permitted.
Close unused tabs after saving their work; resume the video.
If classmates have similar trouble, report a possible connection issue.
why: Streaming relies on available device and network resources.

title: Chromebook Wi-Fi icon shows disconnected
steps: Look at the network indicator near the clock without changing network options.
Tell your teacher if the approved school connection is absent.
Use TechGuide or any already-available offline class resources while waiting.
why: The icon helps distinguish connection loss from a single website error.

title: Chromebook Wi-Fi connected but website fails
steps: Try another teacher-approved class page without entering private information.
If only one site fails, note its exact error; if both fail, tell the teacher.
Do not change proxy, DNS or network settings.
why: This checks whether the fault is specific to one website.

title: Chromebook says offline in Google Docs
steps: Keep the document open and check for the offline or saving indicator.
Copy important work into a teacher-approved location only if your teacher advises it.
Wait for approved connectivity and verify saving before closing.
why: Offline edits may sync later if the app supports it.

title: Chromebook school Wi-Fi asks for sign-in
steps: Stop and show the sign-in prompt to your teacher.
Do not enter your password on an unfamiliar page or choose another network to get around the prompt.
why: Unexpected sign-in pages can be legitimate or unsafe; school staff must verify them.

title: Chromebook read text aloud
steps: Ask your teacher whether Select-to-speak or another reading support is already approved and enabled.
If an approved Select-to-speak control is available, use it to select the assigned text and listen.
Ask for help if the control is missing rather than changing accessibility settings.
why: Text-to-speech can support reading without producing assignment answers.

title: Chromebook screen reader is speaking
steps: Check whether a screen reader is expected for your approved accommodations.
Tell your teacher if speech is unexpected; do not disable it or use accessibility toggle shortcuts.
why: Screen reading can be an essential access tool.

title: Chromebook captions for a class video
steps: Look for CC or subtitles in the teacher-assigned video player.
Choose an available caption track; if unavailable, ask the teacher for an accessible version.
why: Captions provide text for spoken audio and may vary in accuracy.

title: Chromebook need larger text for reading
steps: Use the assigned app's zoom control or browser page zoom to a comfortable level.
Tell your teacher if this is needed regularly or if the entire desktop needs adjustment.
why: App zoom is reversible; system accessibility should follow approved accommodations.

title: Chromebook on-screen keyboard appears
steps: If the Chromebook is a convertible, check whether it is in tablet position.
Tap outside the text field if appropriate; ask the teacher if the keyboard blocks work.
Do not change accessibility keyboard settings yourself.
why: An on-screen keyboard may be a model feature or an accommodation.

title: Chromebook use dictation for own words
steps: Ask your teacher whether voice typing is allowed for the assignment.
In the assigned editor, use its approved voice typing control if already available and speak your own words.
Read back and correct the transcription; ask for help if permission is required.
why: Dictation transcribes your speech rather than writing the assignment for you.

title: Chromebook keyboard focus indicator
steps: Check whether Tab moves the outline to the next control.
Use Enter or Space only when you know which item is selected.
If the outline is unexpected or distracting, ask your teacher; do not disable accessibility controls.
why: Focus indicators show where keyboard input will go.

title: Chromebook tablet mode display
steps: If your device has a convertible hinge, place it in a teacher-approved position without forcing it.
Use the touchscreen in tablet mode if supported or return it gently to laptop position.
If the keyboard remains unavailable, ask your teacher.
why: Some convertible models disable the keyboard when folded.

title: Chromebook sign in to own school account
steps: Select the account assigned to you or enter your school email on the normal sign-in screen.
Enter your own password privately; never tell TechGuide or classmates your password.
If sign-in fails, contact the teacher instead of switching to another person's account.
why: Managed school devices require authorized accounts.

title: Chromebook wrong account showing
steps: Do not open or inspect files from the other account.
Tell your teacher; after they confirm it is appropriate, return to the sign-in screen and choose your own account.
why: Account separation protects student work and privacy.

title: Chromebook forgotten password
steps: Tell your teacher you cannot sign in, without sharing any old password.
Use only the school-approved account recovery process with staff assistance.
TechGuide cannot recover, reset or reveal school passwords.
why: Account recovery requires authorized staff.

title: Chromebook assignment tab says access denied
steps: Check that you opened the exact teacher-provided link and are using your own school account.
Show the message to the teacher; do not request broad permissions or try other accounts.
why: A site may require an assigned account or teacher access approval.

title: Chromebook looks different from teacher demo
steps: Identify the app and look for the equivalent named button or menu in your version.
Ask your teacher if the expected control is not present; do not update software yourself.
why: Device models and app versions can differ.

title: Chromebook unknown app asks to install
steps: Do not approve the installation or open the download.
Show the message to your teacher and use the approved class resource instead.
why: Unexpected installers can be unsafe or prohibited.

title: Chromebook print a school document
steps: Ask the teacher whether printing is allowed for this assignment.
In the document press Ctrl + P, select only the approved printer and inspect the preview.
Confirm the page count and print only with permission; ask staff if the printer is missing.
why: Print preview reduces accidental extra pages and wrong-printer jobs.

title: Chromebook save a permitted page as PDF
steps: Ask whether a PDF is the required submission format.
Open the app's print preview and choose Save to PDF if it is available and permitted.
Name your own file and verify the saved PDF before submitting.
why: PDF captures a fixed layout and may not preserve editable features.

title: Chromebook safely use school USB storage
steps: Get permission to use the approved USB drive and insert it without forcing the connector.
Open Files and locate the drive; copy only your own assigned work.
Use the eject icon in Files before removing it when copying is complete.
why: Ejecting allows pending file writes to finish.

title: Wired mouse disconnects repeatedly
steps: Save your work if you can.
With permission, reconnect only your own accessible mouse plug without forcing it.
If it disconnects again, show the teacher the cable and connector.
why: A loose cable or worn connector can cause intermittent input.

title: Wireless mouse has no power
steps: Check the mouse's own power switch.
Ask the teacher to check the battery or supply an approved spare.
Do not open the mouse or remove a leaking battery.
why: Wireless mice need battery power as well as a working link.

title: Wireless mouse receiver missing
steps: Look at your own mouse and the assigned computer for its small labeled receiver.
Do not take a receiver from another station.
Tell the teacher the mouse is missing its matching receiver.
why: Some wireless mice need a particular receiver to communicate.

title: Mouse pointer jumps around
steps: Move your mouse to a clean, flat, non-glossy surface.
Check for hair or dirt near the sensor without opening the mouse.
If the pointer still jumps, ask for help testing a spare.
why: Optical sensors can struggle with reflective or uneven surfaces.

title: Mouse pointer moves very slowly
steps: Try moving the mouse across a larger clear area.
Test whether the pointer is slow in another approved app.
Ask staff to check the mouse if it is still slow. Do not adjust system sensitivity.
why: Slow movement may be a device issue or an app that is busy.

title: Mouse pointer moves too fast
steps: Move the mouse gently on a flat surface.
If the mouse has an unfamiliar sensitivity button, ask the teacher before touching it.
Tell the teacher if the pointer is difficult to control.
why: Some mice have hardware sensitivity controls that differ by model.

title: Mouse clicks twice by itself
steps: Try a single click on an empty area of your own document.
Check if it occurs in more than one app.
Ask the teacher to test another mouse rather than changing click settings.
why: A worn switch can register extra clicks.

title: Mouse left click not responding
steps: Try a normal single click on a visible button in your own app.
Check if the other button works, without selecting unfamiliar options.
Report which buttons work to the teacher.
why: Identifying the affected button helps isolate the problem.

title: Mouse right-click menu missing
steps: Try right-clicking a harmless item in your own folder.
Some apps use their own menus or ignore right-clicks.
If right-click fails everywhere, tell your teacher.
why: Context menus depend on both the button and the selected object.

title: Accidentally dragging instead of clicking
steps: Release the mouse button completely.
Rest your hand lightly and press once without moving the mouse.
If objects moved accidentally, use the app's Undo if appropriate.
why: A held button plus movement usually starts a drag.

title: Mouse cursor disappears while typing
steps: Move the mouse slightly over the document.
If a selection tool is active, check whether its cursor looks different.
If the pointer never returns, ask your teacher.
why: Some apps hide the pointer during typing or change its appearance for tools.

title: Mouse pointer looks like a spinning circle
steps: Wait briefly for the app to finish processing.
Avoid repeated clicks while it is busy.
If it resumes, save your work. Otherwise ask your teacher.
why: The busy cursor can indicate an operation is still running.

title: Only one keyboard key fails
steps: Test the key in an empty text field in an approved app.
Check whether the key is visibly stuck without prying it up.
Tell the teacher which key fails and whether other keys work.
why: A single failed key can indicate a physical problem.

title: Keyboard repeats letters
steps: Release the key fully and try a short tap in an empty field.
Check whether it occurs with several keys or just one.
Ask your teacher to test the keyboard. Do not change repeat settings.
why: Held or worn keys may produce repeated characters.

title: Keyboard types symbols instead of numbers
steps: Check whether either Shift key is held down.
Release Shift and test a number in a blank field.
If it continues, tell the teacher rather than changing keyboard layouts.
why: Shift changes what the number row types on many keyboards.

title: Keyboard letters in wrong places
steps: Compare what a few keys type in a blank field with their labels.
Check whether a modifier key is stuck.
Tell the teacher if the layout looks wrong. Do not change language or layout settings.
why: A mismatched layout or held key can change characters.

title: Spacebar not typing spaces
steps: Try the spacebar in an editable text field.
Check whether other typing works there.
Tell the teacher if the spacebar still fails. Do not remove keys.
why: The issue may be a single key rather than the whole keyboard.

title: Backspace versus Delete key
steps: Place the cursor inside sample text in your own document.
Backspace removes the character before the cursor; Delete removes the character after it.
Use Undo if you remove the wrong text.
why: These keys work in different directions when editing text.

title: Enter key does not start a new line
steps: Check whether you are in a document, a form or a chat box.
In a document, Enter normally starts a new paragraph.
In a chat or form, it may submit. Check the app's instructions before testing.
why: Enter behavior depends on the application.

title: Tab key jumps to another box
steps: Check whether you are typing in a form or a document.
In a form, Tab generally moves to the next control.
Use the app's indent button if your assignment requires an indent.
why: Tab is also a keyboard navigation control.

title: Arrow keys scroll instead of moving cursor
steps: Click inside the editable text you want to move through.
Try one arrow key in that text.
If a spreadsheet still scrolls while a cell is selected, ask the teacher to check its navigation mode.
why: Arrow keys may navigate a page or an editable selection.

title: Ctrl shortcut is not working
steps: Click inside the app and select the item you intend to use.
Hold Ctrl, tap the other key once, then release both.
If other shortcuts fail too, tell your teacher which ones you tried.
why: Shortcuts depend on keyboard focus and the selected item.

title: Escape from an open menu
steps: Press Esc once while the menu is open.
If the menu stays open, click outside it without choosing a command.
Check that you are back in your document.
why: Escape often cancels a menu or dialog without applying changes.

title: Sticky or jammed keyboard key
steps: Stop pressing the stuck key repeatedly.
Tell your teacher which key is stuck.
Do not pull off the key or spray liquid into the keyboard.
why: Physical cleaning and repair belong to staff.

title: Keyboard cable does not fit
steps: Stop if the plug does not slide in gently.
Compare its shape with the labeled approved port.
Ask the teacher to connect it if you are unsure.
why: Forcing a connector can damage its pins or port.

title: Monitor says no signal
steps: Check whether the computer appears powered on.
Check the monitor's power indicator.
Show the teacher the No signal message. Ask them to check the assigned cable and input source.
why: A powered monitor may not be receiving a video signal.

title: Monitor shows wrong input
steps: Read the input name shown on the monitor.
Tell the teacher which computer and monitor are assigned to you.
Ask the teacher to select the correct input or check cables. Do not change other display controls.
why: The display may be listening to a different video connector.

title: Monitor flickers or flashes
steps: Look away if the flashing causes discomfort.
Save your work only if you can do so comfortably.
Tell your teacher and ask to use another station. Do not adjust refresh settings.
why: Flicker may come from several hardware or display issues.

title: Colored lines on monitor
steps: Check whether the lines appear in more than one approved app.
If possible, show the teacher the screen directly.
Do not press on the screen or rearrange display cables.
why: Lines may indicate a monitor, cable or graphics problem.

title: Monitor image is blurry
steps: Check whether only one image or all desktop text looks blurry.
If only one image is blurry, inspect its original size in the app.
If everything is blurry, ask the teacher. Do not change display resolution.
why: Image quality problems differ from display-wide problems.

title: Monitor picture looks stretched
steps: Check whether other windows are also stretched.
Show your teacher the display and describe when it began.
Do not adjust display resolution or scaling yourself.
why: An incorrect display mode or app layout can distort the picture.

title: Monitor color looks unusual
steps: Check whether the color change affects more than one app.
Tell your teacher if it makes artwork hard to judge.
Do not change system color profiles, accessibility filters or monitor calibration.
why: Color appearance depends on display and app settings.

title: Monitor shows a cracked screen
steps: Stop using the damaged screen.
Tell the teacher immediately and keep hands away from broken glass.
Do not press on it or try to repair it.
why: Broken screens may have sharp edges and require replacement.

title: Second monitor missing
steps: Check whether the second display has a power indicator.
See whether your app is open on the visible display.
Ask the teacher to check display connections or modes. Do not alter display settings.
why: Multiple displays depend on approved classroom configuration.

title: Window is on another monitor
steps: If both displays are working, locate the app on the other display.
Drag its title bar onto your intended screen if you can see it.
If the display is not visible, ask your teacher to recover it.
why: Extended desktops can place windows on different displays.

title: Projector not showing computer
steps: Leave projector cables and controls alone unless directed.
Tell the teacher whether your own monitor shows the correct work.
Ask the teacher to check the assigned projection connection.
why: Classroom projection is shared equipment controlled by staff.

title: Sound plays from speakers instead of headphones
steps: Pause the sound so it does not disturb the class.
Check that your approved headset is connected fully.
If it still plays through speakers, ask the teacher or choose the assigned headset within the app if the app offers it.
why: Audio can be routed to a device other than the one you intended.

title: Headphones only play on one side
steps: Lower the volume.
Check that the plug is fully seated and that the headset is worn correctly.
Test a teacher-approved sound; if one side still fails, report it.
why: A partial connection or damaged headset can affect one channel.

title: Headphones sound crackly
steps: Turn down the volume and pause playback.
Check that the plug is secure without twisting or forcing it.
If the noise remains, ask the teacher to test a spare headset.
why: Connection or device problems can produce unwanted noise.

title: Headphones are too quiet
steps: Check the headset's own volume wheel if it has one.
Check the playback volume inside the app.
Raise volume in small amounts only. If it is still too quiet, ask the teacher.
why: The headset and app may have separate volume controls.

title: Headphones are too loud
steps: Remove the headset if the sound is uncomfortable.
Pause playback and lower the ordinary volume control.
Resume only at a comfortable low level.
why: Keeping volume comfortable protects hearing.

title: Windows volume muted
steps: Click the speaker icon on the taskbar.
If muted, use its normal mute button to restore sound at low volume.
Check whether the approved app also has its own mute control.
why: The taskbar and the app can mute sound separately.

title: Audio works in one app but not another
steps: Check the quiet app's playback and mute controls.
If the sound is in a browser, check the site's player and whether the tab is muted.
If it still fails, tell the teacher which app has sound and which does not.
why: Separate apps can have separate playback controls.

title: Headset microphone arm is in wrong position
steps: With permission, position the adjustable mic near the side of your mouth.
Check the physical mute control.
Try the approved app's microphone test if the teacher permits.
why: Microphone position and mute can affect speech pickup.

title: Microphone sounds very quiet
steps: Check that the mic opening is not covered and the mic is near you.
Speak normally during a teacher-approved test.
If it remains quiet, tell the teacher rather than changing input gain.
why: Distance and obstruction affect microphone volume.

title: Microphone makes an echo
steps: Reduce speaker volume or pause the call if needed.
Use the approved headset instead of playing the call through shared speakers.
Tell the teacher if the echo continues.
why: Speakers can feed sound back into a nearby microphone.

title: Wrong microphone selected in an app
steps: Open the approved meeting or recording app's device chooser if available.
Select the teacher-assigned microphone by its name.
If the name is unclear or access is blocked, ask the teacher.
why: App-level device selection can differ from the computer's default.

title: Webcam image is blurry
steps: Check that the lens cover is fully open with permission.
Make sure the subject is not too close to the camera.
Ask your teacher to clean the lens if needed, without touching it yourself.
why: Obstruction, distance or smudges can reduce camera clarity.

title: Webcam image is too dark
steps: Check that the allowed light is facing the subject, not behind them.
Check whether the lens cover is partly closed.
Ask the teacher if the image is still dark. Do not change camera system settings.
why: Lighting matters for camera exposure.

title: Webcam says in use by another app
steps: Save work in any other approved app using the camera.
Close that app normally if the teacher allows it.
Return to the intended app and try once more.
why: Some camera devices cannot be shared by multiple apps at once.

title: Camera or microphone permission denied
steps: Stop at the permission message.
Show your teacher which app requested access.
Do not change browser or Windows permissions yourself.
why: School staff decide which apps can use recording devices.

title: Identify a USB-A connector
steps: Look at the wide rectangular plug and matching labeled port.
Use only the assigned school device and an accessible approved port.
If the plug does not fit gently, stop and ask the teacher.
why: USB-A plugs have a specific orientation.

title: Identify a USB-C connector
steps: Look for a small rounded oval connector.
Check with your teacher that the port and cable are intended for this device.
Never force the cable or assume it supports every function.
why: USB-C describes connector shape, not all supported functions.

title: Identify an HDMI connector
steps: Look for a video cable labeled HDMI with a wide tapered plug.
Do not unplug classroom monitor or projector cables.
Ask staff to identify the correct connection.
why: HDMI commonly carries picture and sound.

title: Identify a DisplayPort connector
steps: Look for a video cable labeled DP or DisplayPort.
Some plugs have a latch. Leave removal to the teacher.
Ask staff which display connection your station uses.
why: DisplayPort and HDMI are different connectors.

title: Identify a headphone and microphone jack
steps: Look for a headphone or microphone symbol on the assigned computer.
Ask the teacher which port matches your headset, especially if it has one combined plug.
Do not force a plug into an unfamiliar jack.
why: Audio jacks may be separate or combined.

title: USB connector feels loose
steps: Stop pulling or wiggling the connector.
Tell your teacher which accessible port and device are involved.
Do not bend or repair the port yourself.
why: A damaged port can worsen if stressed.

title: USB hub not working
steps: Check whether the assigned hub visibly has power if it has an indicator.
Save your work if possible.
Ask the teacher to inspect the hub and its connection; do not unplug shared devices.
why: Several peripherals may depend on one hub.

title: File Explorer cannot see flash drive
steps: Use the assigned drive only.
Open File Explorer with Windows + E and select This PC.
If the drive is absent, ask the teacher. Do not format or install anything.
why: A recognized storage device should normally appear under This PC.

title: USB asks to format drive
steps: Cancel the format prompt without accepting it.
Tell the teacher what the message says and whether the drive contains work.
Do not try repair or formatting options.
why: Formatting can erase files.

title: USB drive is read-only
steps: Keep the original files unchanged.
Save a copy to your teacher-assigned school folder instead if permitted.
Ask the teacher about the drive's restriction.
why: Read-only storage may protect existing files or reflect school policy.

title: USB file copy is slow
steps: Wait while the transfer progress is moving.
Do not pull out the drive during copying.
If it stops progressing or reports an error, ask the teacher.
why: Interrupting a write can damage the transferred file.

title: Safely eject a Windows flash drive
steps: Finish copying and close files opened from your approved drive.
Use the taskbar's Safely Remove Hardware icon if available, and select your drive.
Wait for confirmation. If unavailable or busy, ask the teacher before unplugging.
why: Ejecting helps protect pending writes.

title: USB says device is in use
steps: Close your own files and windows that are using the drive.
Wait a moment and retry normal Eject.
If it still reports use, ask your teacher before disconnecting.
why: Open files can prevent safe removal.

title: Flash drive is full
steps: Save the current project to your assigned school storage if possible.
Do not delete unknown or other people's files.
Ask the teacher which storage location to use.
why: A drive needs free space for new files.

title: Drawing tablet is connected but cursor will not move
steps: Check that the pen matches the assigned tablet.
